1 Cite as

Lars Vilhuber, 2025, “Code and Data for: Reproducibility and Open Science in Economics”, Zenodo, V1, https://doi.org/10.1234/something

2 Overview

The code in this replication package constructs most tables and figures from outside data sources. The code is in R. The replication package also includes PNG and PDF copies of screenshots and external figures, as noted below.

3 Data Availability and Provenance Statements

All data are public, and can be redistributed.

3.1 Statement about Rights

3.2 License for Data

  • Data fom Crossref (2023) is “is open and available for reuse without restriction” (https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/)

All derivative data contained herein, if not otherwise encumbered, is available under a CC-BY-NC-4.0 license. Usage by commercial entities is permitted, reselling the data is not.

3.5.2 Access statistics for AEA journals

The access statistics were extracted by me from internal AEA systems used by the AEA Data Editor. Similar statistics are published in Vilhuber (2025). The direct extracts are confidential and not provided, but the code produces distributable data, which are included here.

3.5.3 Crossref data

Data were accessed in 2024 (Crossref 2023). The CrossRef database is described in Hendricks et al. (2020). CrossRef data are accessed via an API, and can be updated over time. The derived data are included in this deposit. I use a hand-curated list of ISSNs to identify publishers.

Data Source Filename Provided
CrossRef ./data/crossref_dois_enhanced.Rds TRUE
CrossRef ./data/crossref_dois.Rds TRUE

3.5.6 NSF Doctorate Recipients National Science Foundation (2024)

The Excel file was downloaded in January 2025, and was created in 2024 by the National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics. Numbers were manually inserted into the text. Data published by the NSF is habitually in the public domain, no copyright is claimed in the United States.

Data Source Filename Provided
NSF (2024) ./data/nsf24336-tab001-005.xlsx TRUE

3.5.7 U.S. Census Bureau (2024)

The Excel file with participants in Census Bureau-related research projects was downloaded in January 2025 from Github. As of June 2025, the Github repository had been made private. Data published by the U.S. Census Bureau is habitually in the public domain, no copyright is claimed in the United States.

Data Source Filename Provided
U.S. Census Bureau (2024) ./data/ProjectsAllMetadata_25JUN2024.xlsx TRUE

3.5.8 Data on Norwegian economists

The data on Norwegian economists was obtained from the RePEc page IDEAS//RePEc (2025), and manually transcribed.

Data on the number of NBER affiliates was observed from the NBER website National Bureau of Economic Research (2025), and manually transcribed.

3.5.10 Data on J-PAL affiliates

Data on the number of J-PAL affiliates was observed from the J-PAL website Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (2025) and manually transcribed.

Stata licenses were obtained in June 2025 from the StataCorp website. Laptop prices were observed on HP.com website for the USA and Germany for roughly similar models, and on Shopee.vn for Vietnam. A screenshot for Vietnam is included.

5 Description of programs/code

Each numbered R program can be run independently, in the sequence implied by the numbering scheme. A convenience bash main script (run.sh) to run all programs is provided in the root of the project, and will run all data cleaning and analysis programs.

Of note, several programs leverage APIs, which can yield different results, and might take long time. The programs will detect previously downloaded data files, and skip the download part if those files are present. To start with a fresh download, delete the following files:

Internet access is required to run the programs,

  • to download the key input files

5.1 License for Code

The code (all files ending in .R, .Rmd, and .sh) is licensed under a BSD license. See LICENSE.txt for details.

6 Instructions to Replicators

If using Docker image on Linux or macOS system:

  • run start_rstudio.sh and connect to https://localhost:8787
  • in the “Terminal” of the RStudio app, run bash ./run.sh

or equivalently,

  • in the terminal of a computer with Docker installed, run bash ./run_docker.sh ./run.sh

Alternative ways to run this (these were not tested):

  • optionally, before running project code, run Rscript -e "renv::restore()" (on Windows, Rscript.exe -e "renv::restore()" ) to isolate the project libraries from your system (assumes renv is installed, see renv).
  • Using the same R version as described above, run each program individually as desired, in the order indicated above.

6.1 Details

Filename Note
config.R Basic configuration
code/libraries.R Defines libraries used globally in various pieces (data acquisition, analysis)

code/02_convert_tables.R Converts variables tables from Excel to LaTeX
code/03_tabulate_access_aea.R Reads private AEA data and writes cleaned data
code/04_tabulate_access_categories.R Tabulate AEA access outcomes
code/11_get_crossref.R Get full list of NBER publications, print out in-text numbers.
code/13_analyse_authors.R Unduplicates authors, prints out in-text numbers
code/20_geocode_stata_step1.R Uses data provided by Kit Baum and writes out intermediate file
code/21_geocode_stata_step2.R Uses Geolite database and host command to identify geography of IP addresses
code/22_generate_download_map.R Uses geocoded download data to create map.
code/25_download_R_logs.R Download Posit/CRAN logs
code/26_aggregate_data.R Aggregates Posit/CRAN data by country
code/27_map_R_by_country.R Creates maps, and computes regional statistics for R download
code/28_stata_map_by_country.R Creates maps, and computes regional statistics for Stata download
code/29_compare_stata_r_by_region.R Loads the regional and North/South statistics from the R and Stata analyses, # computes the percent difference, and outputs combined tables and a horizontal histogram of differences.
